Trace, implement and test: Counting Sort

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"
)

func CountingSort(nums []int, min, max int) {
	n := len(nums)
	k := max - min + 1
	c := make([]int, k)
	for _, v := range nums {
		c[v-min]++
	}
	log.Println(c)

	for i := 1; i < k; i++ {
		c[i] += c[i-1]
	}
	log.Println(c)

	r := make([]int, n)
	for i := n - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		v := nums[i]
		a := c[v-min]
		r[a-1] = v
		c[v-min]--
		log.Println(r)
	}

	for i, v := range r {
		nums[i] = v
	}
	log.Println(nums)
}

func main() {
	// uncomment following line to enable log print
	// log.SetOutput(io.Discard)

	// test case 1
	nums := []int{1, 2, 7, 9, 5, 5, 8}
	CountingSort(nums, 1, 9)
	fmt.Println(nums)

	// wait complete output to terminal
	time.Sleep(time.Second)

	// test case 2
	nums = []int{3, 7, 9, 5, 5, 8, 11}
	CountingSort(nums, 3, 11)
	fmt.Println(nums)
}
